title: Claude Code plugin (skills, subagents, hooks, manifest)

rules.rule: Reference bundled files as ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/... written in the skill or agent Markdown body (substituted at load), never as $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT inside a Bash command the model runs.
rules.why: The path variables are not present in the environment of commands Claude runs through the Bash tool, in the main session or a subagent; an env-var reference expands to an empty string and the command reads or runs the wrong path.

rules.rule: Call the helper CLI as bare `stackfoundry` (bin/ is on the Bash tool's PATH while the plugin is enabled) and keep the `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/stackfoundry"` fallback where a skill already names it.
rules.why: bin/ is only on PATH while the plugin is enabled, and claude.ai and Cowork do not install a plugin that has a top-level bin/ directory; without the fallback a skill's CLI step fails with command-not-found on those surfaces.

rules.rule: Never write state under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}; durable plugin-side state goes in ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}, repo state in the user's repo.
rules.why: ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} points at cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/, changes with every version and the old directory is deleted 14 days after an update; anything written there is lost.
where: not used here yet (skills write only into the user's repo under .claude/stackfoundry/ and docsRoot)

rules.rule: Everything a skill, agent or hook reads at run time must live inside plugins/stackfoundry/; never reach above the plugin root (../) from a component or script.
rules.why: Marketplace installs copy only the plugin directory into the cache; a path above the root is not found for installed users, and a component path that escapes the root fails validation and does not load.
where: plugins/stackfoundry/evals/README.md (fixtures/ at the repo root: evals must run from a clone, not an installed copy)

rules.rule: Bump plugin.json `version` in every release that should reach users.
rules.why: A manifest-pinned version keeps every user on the cached copy until the string changes, however many commits are pushed; `claude plugin update` reports 'already at the latest version'.

rules.rule: Keep userConfig options to the documented keys (type, title, description, required, default, options, multiple, sensitive, min, max) and read values as ${user_config.KEY} in skill or agent content; in a shell-form hook read CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY> from the environment instead.
rules.why: userConfig options are strict: an unknown key makes the plugin fail to load. Shell-form hook commands reject ${user_config.*} and the hook errors instead of running. A `sensitive` value is replaced by a placeholder in skill and agent content.

rules.rule: Using `options` on a userConfig field requires Claude Code v2.1.271+; state that floor wherever the plugin's requirements are documented, and do not add a newer-only manifest feature without raising it.
rules.why: Users on Claude Code before v2.1.271 cannot load a plugin that declares `options` on any field: the whole plugin fails, not just the setting.

rules.rule: Give every agent an explicit `tools:` grant that covers exactly what its body tells it to call; leaf roles omit `Agent`, read-only roles omit Edit/Write.
rules.why: An agent without `tools` inherits every tool available to subagents, and by default a subagent can spawn its own subagents up to three layers deep; a read-only role then edits the user's repo or fans out uncontrolled.
rules.repoConvention: The repo enforces this with verify-plumbing and .claude/rules/authoring.md (grants cover the ## Tooling section; read-only roles never get Edit/Write).

rules.rule: Do not put `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `permissionMode` or `initialPrompt` in a plugin agent's frontmatter; ship hooks in hooks/hooks.json and MCP servers in .mcp.json at plugin level.
rules.why: For security reasons Claude Code ignores these fields when loading agents from a plugin, silently, so a guard or permission mode the author relied on never applies.

rules.rule: Questions for the user are asked by the dispatching skill, never by an agent: agents return `questions` in their report.
rules.why: AskUserQuestion is always removed from subagents, even when `tools` is omitted; an agent told to ask stalls or guesses.

rules.rule: Put every fact an agent needs in its dispatch brief (paths, versions, risk, output path); do not rely on the skill's conversation.
rules.why: A subagent starts with a fresh context: it does not see the parent conversation or the invoking skill's content (only CLAUDE.md, git status and its own prompt), so an unstated fact is guessed.

rules.rule: Keep `disable-model-invocation: true` off skills that are scheduled or preloaded into agents; use it only for skills a person starts on purpose.
rules.why: The flag also blocks preloading into subagents and running from a session-scoped scheduled task, so a scheduled skill carrying it never runs.
where: plugins/stackfoundry/skills/schedule/SKILL.md (registers check-updates, tech-radar, stackfoundry-radar, flaky-watch, docs-reconciler: none set the flag)
rules.repoConvention: .claude/rules/authoring.md: slash-only skills set disable-model-invocation: true (init, upgrade, schedule, configure-guards, materialize, act-on-*, github-prs, elaborate-plan).

rules.rule: Treat `allowed-tools` as a pre-approval grant, not a restriction; to remove tools while a skill runs use `disallowed-tools`.
rules.why: allowed-tools lets the listed tools run without a permission prompt for the turn and leaves every unlisted tool callable; adding Bash or Write there to 'limit' a skill silently widens what runs unprompted in the user's repo.
where: not used here yet (no skill sets allowed-tools)

rules.rule: Keep SKILL.md bodies short and move shared detail to reference/ files linked by path.
rules.why: The rendered SKILL.md stays in context for the rest of the session and is not re-read; after compaction only the first 5,000 tokens of each recent skill are re-attached within a combined 25,000-token budget, so long skills lose their tail and older skills drop out.

rules.rule: Write skill descriptions without angle brackets and keep them within the repo caps (250 skills, 300 agents).
rules.why: Angle brackets < and > display as HTML entities in the skill listing; descriptions are always in context, and combined agent descriptions over 15,000 tokens trigger a startup warning.
rules.repoConvention: Docs truncate description + when_to_use at 1,536 characters; this repo caps far lower (250/300) in .claude/rules/authoring.md and enforces it in verify-plumbing. Follow the repo.

rules.rule: Return PreToolUse decisions as hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision (deny/ask/allow/defer) with permissionDecisionReason and exit 0; never the top-level decision/reason fields.
rules.why: Top-level decision/reason are deprecated for PreToolUse; exit code 1 without valid JSON is a non-blocking error and the call proceeds.

rules.rule: In shell-form hook commands wrap ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in double quotes, and keep the hook fast (timeout seconds, it runs on every matched tool call).
rules.why: An unquoted path with spaces splits into several words (claude plugin validate warns); a slow guard delays every Edit, Write and shell call.

rules.rule: Normalise Windows paths before matching a hook's file_path against globs, and decode hook stdin as UTF-8 bytes.
rules.why: On Windows the Write/Edit/Read path arrives with backslash separators; a glob written with '/' then never matches and a protected file is editable.

rules.rule: Do not treat the PreToolUse guard as the enforcement boundary: a hard deny belongs in permission rules; the hook is a guardrail.
rules.why: The hooks docs say to use the permission system rather than a hook to enforce a hard allow or deny; a hook that cannot start, times out or prints invalid output lets the call go through unless onFailure is 'block'.
rules.repoConvention: The guard fails open on purpose (hooks.json description: 'No profile, no opinion; if the hook itself cannot run (no sh or Python), the call goes through'), so a missing toolchain never wedges a user's session. Follow the repo; see questions.

bugCategories.name: plugin-path-resolution
bugCategories.lookFor: $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT used as an env var in a Bash command a skill tells Claude to run; ../ paths from plugin files; a ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/ link to a file that does not exist; state written under the plugin root; backslash component paths.
bugCategories.failure: The installed plugin reads an empty or missing path (works from a clone, breaks for marketplace users), or loses state on the next update.

bugCategories.name: tool-grant-drift
bugCategories.lookFor: An agent whose body (## Tooling) calls a tool missing from `tools:`, a read-only role granted Edit/Write, an agent with no `tools:`, a leaf role granted Agent, a skill told to ask the user from inside an agent.
bugCategories.failure: The role cannot do its job (tool call refused), or it writes to or fans out across the user's repo beyond its role.

bugCategories.name: silently-ignored-frontmatter
bugCategories.lookFor: Frontmatter keys Claude Code ignores (unknown keys, hooks/mcpServers/permissionMode/initialPrompt in plugin agents), and YAML that may not parse (unquoted colons, brackets in argument-hint).
bugCategories.failure: If the YAML does not parse the skill loads with no fields set, so a slash-only skill loses disable-model-invocation and Claude can start a repo-writing skill on its own; ignored agent fields drop a guard without any error.

bugCategories.name: hook-unintended-fail-open
bugCategories.lookFor: Guard paths that exit non-zero (other than 2) or print non-JSON to stdout, unhandled exceptions, slow work near the timeout, path comparisons not normalised for Windows, non-UTF-8 stdin decoding, matchers that miss a tool name (PowerShell, NotebookEdit).
bugCategories.failure: A generated file the profile protects is hand-edited, or a forbidden command runs, with no visible block.

bugCategories.name: unreleased-change
bugCategories.lookFor: Changes under plugins/stackfoundry/ merged for release without a plugin.json version bump and CHANGELOG entry.
bugCategories.failure: Users stay on the old cached copy; `claude plugin update` reports already at the latest version.

bugCategories.name: brief-context-gap
bugCategories.lookFor: A dispatch (subagent_type) whose brief omits a fact the agent's body requires (output path, versions, target, risk), or an agent body that refers to 'the conversation' or 'what the user said'.
bugCategories.failure: The subagent starts with a fresh context, guesses the missing fact and writes a wrong pack, report or file.

bugCategories.name: untrusted-content-as-instructions
bugCategories.lookFor: A role that reads user repo files or fetched pages without saying their instructions are data; skill output from !`command` built from repo-controlled values; a skill that passes report text from one agent to another as instructions.
bugCategories.failure: Prompt injection planted in a user's repo or a web page steers a role into editing, committing or exfiltrating; subagent output scanning only marks instruction-like text and does not remove it.

bugCategories.name: userconfig-substitution
bugCategories.lookFor: ${user_config.KEY} naming a key not declared in plugin.json, used in a shell-form hook or monitor, or naming a sensitive option in skill content; unknown keys inside a userConfig option.
bugCategories.failure: The plugin fails to load (strict option object), the hook errors instead of running, or the skill sees a placeholder instead of the value.

testing.layers: Static: unittest (tests/) for the helper CLI and guard, verify-plumbing for skill/agent frontmatter, grants and links, `claude plugin validate --strict` for the manifests. Behaviour: `claude plugin eval` cases under evals/ compare with- and without-plugin arms on scaffolded fixture repos.
commands: cd plugins/stackfoundry && claude plugin eval . --scaffold --runs 1 --no-publish --tag read-only
traps: A single eval run is noisy: iterate with --runs 1, but confirm at the default 3 runs before trusting a change.
Pin --model (and the judge model) when running evals in CI so a model rollout is not read as a plugin regression; pass --trust-plugin so the job never waits at the trust prompt.
Hooks run outside the agent's sandbox and can change the files graders read: treat eval scores of hook cases as advisory unless run in an isolated runner.
To assert a tool was never called use a tool_used grader with both min: 0 and max: 0.
`claude plugin validate --strict` results depend on the CLI version; keep the CI pin and re-run after bumping it.

wiring.check: Every ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/<path> in a skill or agent body exists under plugins/stackfoundry/.
wiring.failure: The skill reads a missing reference file for installed users.

wiring.check: Every subagent_type "stackfoundry:<name>" names an agents/<name>.md whose `name` equals the file name (plugin agents are addressed as plugin:agent).
wiring.failure: The dispatch fails or falls back to a generic agent without the role's grant.

wiring.check: Every /stackfoundry:<skill> reference names a skills/<skill>/SKILL.md whose `name` equals the folder.
wiring.failure: A skill points the user or another skill at a command that does not exist.

wiring.check: Every ${user_config.KEY} used in skills or agents is declared under plugin.json userConfig, and no option holds an unknown key.
wiring.failure: The skill sees an unsubstituted reference; an unknown option key stops the plugin loading.

wiring.check: hooks/hooks.json wraps its event map in a top-level "hooks" key, and the matcher lists every edit and shell tool the guard handles (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, Bash, PowerShell).
wiring.failure: A file without the wrapper fails to load; a tool missing from the matcher bypasses the guard.

wiring.check: plugin.json `name` stays kebab-case with no reserved prefix, and the marketplace entry `source` (./plugins/stackfoundry) resolves inside the marketplace.
wiring.failure: Validation fails or components are namespaced under an unexpected name.

performance.note: Skill and agent descriptions are always in context; only bodies load on demand. Combined non-built-in agent descriptions over 15,000 tokens trigger a startup warning, so the repo caps keep the plugin's fixed context cost low.
The PreToolUse guard runs on every Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit/Bash/PowerShell call with a 10 s timeout; keep it to a JSON read and a glob match, with no git or network calls.
At most 20 subagents run concurrently by default (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS); wider fan-outs from orchestrator skills queue.

security.note: Every role reads the user's repo and, for researchers and reviewers, web pages: both are prompt-injection surfaces. Roles state that embedded instructions are data and report them; Claude Code's subagent-output scan only marks instruction-like text, never removes it, and is no substitute for restricting what a subagent can reach.
Least privilege per role is the real control: read-only roles without Edit/Write, leaf roles without Agent, WebFetch/WebSearch only for researchers and reviewers that need them.

The guard hook is a guardrail, not an enforcement boundary: it fails open (onFailure continue, internal errors exit 0), and on Windows without Git Bash a shell-form hook runs under PowerShell where `sh` may be missing. Hard denies belong in permission rules (permissions.deny; permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories since 2.1.314).
!`command` dynamic context injection inserts command output as plain text that is not re-scanned; do not build such commands from repo-controlled values (not used here yet).

Skills write into users' repos: a skill's allowed-tools would let those writes run without prompts, and users are told to review allowed-tools of skills before running; keep skills free of allowed-tools grants for Edit/Write/Bash.

lockStep: The CI CLI pin and verify-plumbing's SKILL_KEYS / AGENT_KEYS / IGNORED_IN_PLUGIN_AGENTS / KNOWN_TOOLS sets in plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/plumbing.py: re-check them against the skills and subagents docs when the pin moves.
Minimum user CLI: userConfig `options` needs v2.1.271+, hook `onFailure` needs v2.1.295+.
plugin.json version with plugins/stackfoundry/CHANGELOG.md and the stackfoundry--v<version> tag (docs/release.md).

Hooks reference beyond its first 200,000 characters (security considerations section, plugin-hook trust details) was not read; whether PreToolUse hooks fire for tool calls inside subagents was not confirmed by the docs read.
Skills page beyond its first 100,000 characters and sub-agents page beyond 100,000 characters were not read.
Permissions page (code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions) was not fetched; permission-rule claims come from the hooks, security and changelog pages.
No Claude Code security advisory database was consulted (GitHub advisories for anthropics/claude-code).
questions: The hooks docs say to enforce a hard deny with the permission system, not a hook; the guard is a fail-open PreToolUse hook (hooks.json onFailure: continue). Should init also write permissions.deny rules (for example Edit(...) on generated globs) into the user's .claude/settings.json, or stay hook-only?
The plugin needs Claude Code v2.1.271+ (userConfig options) and v2.1.295+ (onFailure), but no minimum CLI version is stated for users. Document a floor in the plugin README / marketplace description?
The CI pin is 2.1.307 and the latest release is 2.1.319 (2.1.310 fixed Windows PreToolUse hooks letting calls through when Git Bash is missing). Bump the pin?
The guard matcher includes MultiEdit, which the current hooks docs no longer mention. Keep it as harmless, or drop it from the matcher and guard.py EDIT_TOOLS?
